summary.headline: Meesho Q2 FY27 contribution margin rose to about 6%, driven mainly by logistics efficiencies, with management reinvesting part of the gain into pricing.
summary.overview: Management said the contribution margin improvement was led by logistics efficiencies (RTO reduction, higher order density, middle-mile network redesign, Valmo cost gains) rather than ad take-rate. Management cautioned the 6% CM should not be extrapolated, as part of the gain is held back for seller and consumer pricing once server costs normalise. Adjusted EBITDA margin was about minus 1% of NMV, with a quarterly FCF print helped by a roughly INR523 crore working capital release tied to festive-season timing shifting into September. Festive season sales were described as better than expectations, with traffic at all-time highs, though seller-side supply disruptions from crude and Middle East volatility were flagged.

financial_highlights.value: about 6% of NMV (as referenced by analyst)
about INR3 per order, of which about INR4 from logistics cost (as per analyst recap)
financial_highlights.change: revenue per order slightly lower QoQ due to pass-through carry-over

financial_highlights.value: positive, helped by working capital release of about INR523 crore
financial_highlights.change: management says Q2 FY26 showed a similar working-capital pattern

financial_highlights.metric: Fixed cost below CM (1H FY27, as per analyst)
financial_highlights.change: vs 6.3% of NMV in FY26; no leverage yet

segments.name: Logistics / Valmo
segments.commentary: Delivery speed improved about 15%, a trend management expects to continue across Q2 and Q3 combined. Valmo cost of doing business continues to fall, and management says festive capacity and efficiency were good. RTO as a share of orders fell QoQ.

segments.name: Financial services
segments.commentary: Seller and consumer lending products are showing good signs with risk within pricing norms. Bank partners are being added to the NBFC base. AUM and medium-term targets will be shared later, as this is still a new initiative.

guidance_outlook: No specific full-year guidance. FY27 contribution margin expected to be substantially better than FY26, with logistics spread restored toward FY25 levels during the year.
Management retains flexibility on how much logistics gain is passed to sellers and consumers versus retained, as well as on server cost.
Server cost as a percentage of NMV expected to normalise to the baseline by Q4 FY27.
Long-term guidance of about 25% NMV CAGR (five-year, towards FY31) maintained; revisit after FY28 visibility.
Ad monetisation as a percentage of NMV expected to rise, supporting FY28 economics.
Long-run fixed cost base expected to come to about 3% of NMV, per CFO.
capex_capacity: Server/GPU costs elevated in Q2 as capacity for festive season was procured early; management is diversifying providers and regions and buying capacity only when needed.
Automation investments across Valmo nodes are rising; management says most capex is being funded by Valmo partners, not Meesho, and no FCF impact is seen currently.
Middle-mile network redesign, larger trucks and more line-haul shifts drove efficiency; last-mile model unchanged.
New initiatives capped at about INR200 crore annual capital allocation, including Kirana Club, whose acquisition closed just before the call.
demand_pricing: Festive season moved from September (last year) to October this year, creating a base effect on YoY and ATU growth.
LTM ATU additions rose only about 10 million QoQ despite ANP spend up about 50% QoQ; management says marketing is rebalanced on CAC and LTV with ROI still healthy.
Growth adjusted for festive shift was above 30%, even with pricing benefits held back, per analyst recap.
NMV per seller is flat to declining in aggregate due to growth in small non-GST sellers; management says cohorts of large manufacturers are growing well.
Management chose not to charge platform, convenience or handling fees and says it will prefer logistics or ad take-rate increases.

qa_highlights.question: Where should CM settle in 2H and what about FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Dhiresh Bansal said Q2's 6% should not be extrapolated because of lead-lag in passing efficiencies to sellers and consumers. FY27 CM should be substantially better than FY26, and FY28 gains will come from ad monetisation rising as a share of NMV.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin gain is from ad take-rate versus logistics?
qa_highlights.answer: Logistics was the primary driver, covering RTO, density, network redesign and Valmo efficiency. Ad-rate details were not disclosed separately. There were no specific volume-slab pricing changes from 3PLs this quarter; these typically come in the December quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why is growth not being used to keep CM high, and why pass pricing benefit back now?
qa_highlights.answer: Vidit Aatrey said pricing investments pay off over multiple quarters through the flywheel. Passing back CM would not add 10-15% growth immediately, but it makes more categories and sellers viable over the next 12-18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any sign of rising CAC or churn given the ATU growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Vidit said ATU growth partly reflects festive timing. Marketing is reallocated on CAC and LTV, with the same internal hurdle rates, and new-user growth in big cities is nearly as fast as in smaller towns.

qa_highlights.question: Why is fixed cost leverage not showing up, and what is the steady state?
qa_highlights.answer: Dhiresh said Q2 server costs were elevated by GPU capacity bought early for the festive season, with normalisation expected by Q4 FY27. Pre-festive marketing spend also front-loaded costs. Long-run fixed cost is targeted at about 3% of NMV.

qa_highlights.question: Will the working-capital release in Q2 reverse?
qa_highlights.answer: Dhiresh said the Q2 release reflects festive sales spilling into September. Normalised, a 20-day negative working capital cycle and 30% growth should yield about 1.5% of NMV positive FCF, and LTM FCF should turn positive in a few quarters.

risks_watch: Server/GPU cost normalisation to baseline by Q4 FY27; GPU pricing is currently elevated globally.
Reinvestment in pricing could cap CM gains; the logistics gain pass-through is discretionary.
Seller supply disruptions from crude and Middle East volatility, plus macro pressure on household budgets, though management sees no consumer demand weakness yet.
Quarterly FCF is volatile, with the December quarter typically a lean period for NMV.
Fixed costs below CM are not yet leveraging; watch whether FY27 shows operating leverage as management expects.
Financial services AUM, risk metrics and targets to be disclosed later; Kirana Club integration and investment needs are still open.
summary.management_tone: Confident on logistics efficiency, demand and festive performance, while being deliberately non-committal on quarterly CM, full-year numbers and Valmo's share. Management openly signalled that margin gains will be reinvested rather than retained.
key_quotes: So the primary cause for improvement has been on the logistics side and the efficiencies that we have gained there.
We do not see like any concern emerging anywhere.
So if we pass on our CM back tomorrow, like will we suddenly grow by 10%, 15%? The answer is no, because a lot of this is flywheel-related impact.
We generally don't believe in charging any platform fee.

adds.what: Valmo automation investments across nodes (funded mainly by Valmo partners, not Meesho; no FCF impact seen)
Middle-mile network redesign with larger trucks and more line-haul shifts (efficiency, not added capacity)

growth.why: Long-term 25% NMV CAGR (five-year, towards FY31) maintained; FY27 contribution margin guided substantially better than FY26 with logistics spread restored toward FY25 levels, backed by logistics efficiencies (RTO reduction, density, middle-mile redesign) and delivery speed up ~15%, but no specific capacity or orders with numbers and the brief gives no quarterly revenue or EBITDA growth figures.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides FY27 contribution margin substantially better than FY26 with logistics spread restored toward FY25 levels, but Q2's ~6% CM is not to be extrapolated as gains are partly reinvested in pricing; fixed costs ~6.4-6.5% of NMV show no leverage yet and server costs normalise only by Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Festive growth adjusted for the Sept-to-Oct shift was above 30% and delivery speed improved ~15%, with long-term 25% NMV CAGR maintained, though NMV per seller is flat to declining in aggregate due to small non-GST sellers.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is capped at about INR200 crore annually for all new initiatives, Valmo automation is funded by partners with no FCF impact, and no utilisation-driven plant expansion was flagged.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held the 25% five-year NMV CAGR and guided FY27 CM substantially better than FY26, but explicitly refused to extrapolate Q2's ~6% CM and is reinvesting gains.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Server/GPU costs are elevated and normalise only by Q4 FY27, seller supply is exposed to crude and Middle East volatility, and fixed costs are not leveraging yet at 6.4-6.5% of NMV.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Financial services (seller and consumer lending, new bank partners) and Kirana Club are new initiatives, but AUM and targets are not yet disclosed and no product launch dates were given.

rows.label: Logistics spread restored toward FY25 levels
rows.why: Management said it will restore part of the FY26 lost logistics spread toward FY25 levels, driven by RTO reduction, order density and middle-mile redesign, with delivery speed up ~15% expected to continue across Q2 and Q3.

rows.label: Q2 working capital release may not repeat
rows.why: The INR523 crore release reflected festive sales spilling into September, and the 20-day negative cycle implies only about 1.5% of NMV positive FCF once normalised, with December quarter typically lean.

rows.label: Pass-through of logistics gain to sellers and consumers
rows.why: Management said the logistics gain will be held back for seller and consumer pricing once server costs normalise, with no platform, convenience or handling fees charged, and 3PL volume-slab changes typically arrive in the December quarter.

tone.note: Management was confident on logistics efficiency, festive performance and the 25% NMV CAGR, but cautious on not extrapolating the 6% CM and openly reinvesting gains; analysts pushed on CAC and churn with ATU growth, the lack of fixed-cost leverage, and how much of the margin came from ads versus log
